newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Canada seeks Asian investment in mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Canada seeks Asian investment in mining sector.

text.p: Canada's strong economy and solid mining industry made mining an attractive investment for Asian fund managers seeking to diversify portfolios, said Canadian government and business representatives on Tuesday.

"We expect the country's (economic) growth to continue above three percent for the next two to three years," said Dale Hull, director of the economic analysis division for the Minerals and Metals Sector of Natural Resources Canada.
Hall was addressing Asian fund managers at a seminar organised by the Hong Kong Commission for Canada and Natural Resources Canada.
Canada's mining sector had performed well and the country was a vibrant centre for mine financing, he said.
Donald Gordon, marketing director for the Vancouver Stock Exchange, said in his presentation the exchange was well suited for investors seeking rich returns.
The VSE was growing rapidly and in 1996, trading value on the exchange was $12 billion, up 87 percent over 1996 trading value.

Newly developed technology had recently allowed Canada to exploit its rich diamond reserves and resulted in the development of diamond veins at the Lac de Gras on the Arctic frontier, said Harvey Thorleifson, research scientist at the Geological Survey of Canada.

"You get something comparable to the greatest diamond mines in the world, something that's going to produce over ten billion dollars in revenue over a 25-year mining plan," Thorleifson said in his presentation.
